names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 5 Απριλίου, «Άγιοι Θεοδώρα και Δίδυμος», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 27. мај ст. ст., „Свети мученици Теодора и Дидим“ — Свети is not a rank, мученици is the `martyr` in `types`, and Теодора is his companion and not part of his name; the body confirms the bare form in the nominative, „уђе к њој војник по имену Дидим“. **Measured, and it is a fold of two**: `foldchk.py` returns `[('didymus-of-laodicea', 'ru'), ('didymus-of-laodicea', 'sr')]` for «Дидим», so that folder holds the identical string already and this makes a second holder. **There is nothing fuller to prefer**: the heading gives the two companions’ names and nothing else, and Alexandria is the other book’s to attach. The two are told apart by their days — Laodicea on its own — and by this one being half of a pair. The corpus keeps two further Didymi, of Cyprus and the tribune of 24 May met in this same wave, neither holding an `sr` form. The Greek form here, «Δίδυμος», is the same bare name.

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 5 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. It puts the martyrdom «κατά τον πιο άγριο διωγμό της Εκκλησίας, επί Διοκλητιανού» and gives no year at all, so there are no dates here. He is not the Didymus of Laodicea whom the same calendar keeps on 11 September.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 09.06.2026 (27. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети мученици Теодора и Дидим“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry, whose heading names him second. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of the 23 to 27 May is — note that the 7 May and 24 April headings quoted elsewhere in this wave do carry one, so this is the page and not a transcription habit. **A DAY NEITHER OTHER CALENDAR KEEPS THE PAIR ON.** saint.gr keeps them together on 5 April and the Romanian and Russian rows are `undocumented`, so the row is written on the 27/5 and the Greek row is left on the 5/4. The day list for the menologion 27/5 could not see either of them for that reason, and **`sr-namesweep.mjs` found them because the heading prints both names** — the one shape of enumerated company it does manage, two names with the first one scored. **FIRST DATES FOR BOTH, AND THE EMPEROR DISAGREES.** Neither folder has had a `dates` object: the existing life records „The page gives no year, names no relics and prints no hymn under either of them.“ The Prologue states one — „Чесно пострадаше и задобише венце вечне славе 304. године у Александрији“ — so `dates.death` is 304 to 304, `basis: "traditional"`, with the book’s own words in the note. **The reign is used for nothing, and it is the reign the two books differ on**: this entry opens „У време злочестивог цара Максимилијана“, Maximian, where saint.gr puts the martyrdom „in the fiercest persecution the Church knew, under Diocletian“. **No year was derived from either reign and neither emperor was chosen**; both stand in the prose. **AND THE PROLOGUE NAMES NO EPARCH WHERE SAINT.GR NAMES EUSTRATIUS**, calling him only „кнез мучитељ“ and „судија“. Nothing was reconciled: a persecutor gains no folder by the coordinator’s third ruling and the existing life keeps the Greek page’s name for him. **THE EXECUTION IS A DIFFERENT SCENE IN EACH BOOK, AND THIS ONE IS THE DIALOGUE.** saint.gr has Didymus beheaded and burnt, and then Theodora present herself to the eparch, reproach him for the killing and be thrown into the flames. **The Prologue has her run to the place of execution and argue with Didymus himself**: „Иако си ти спасао моју част, ја нисам од тебе искала да ме спасеш од смрти. Уступи мени смрт мученичку!“ — though you saved my honour, I did not ask you to save me from death; yield me the martyr’s death — and his answer, „Возљубљена сестро, не спречавај ме да умрем за Христа и крвљу мојом оперем грехе моје!“ **And the pagans, hearing the quarrel, condemned them both**, and **both were beheaded and both bodies burnt**, where saint.gr has her burnt alive. **Both tellings are written and neither is resolved.** **«сестро» IS NOT A KINSHIP.** He calls her beloved sister at the scaffold and nothing in either book makes them kin; the two folders were already `related` to each other in both directions as companions, and no row was added or changed. No `locations`, although Alexandria is named in both books. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion. **`soldier` ADDED, AND IT IS THIS BOOK’S WORD AND NOT AN INFERENCE FROM THE GREEK PAGE’S.** „уђе к њој војник по имену Дидим“ — a soldier named Didymus came in to her — and Војник maps to `soldier` in BRIEF-SERBIAN.md §5. **saint.gr does not say it**: it makes him „a man of rank at Alexandria“ who „put on his uniform“, from which a reader could have guessed the rank and this corpus did not. **Now it is stated and the type is written.** `soldier` is **not in `src/lib/honorific.js`’s `PRECEDENCE`**, so the page goes on reading *Martyr Didymus* off the `martyr` he already carries and the new word shows only in the facts line. **Of him in particular, new besides**: that **he told her he too was a servant of Christ**; that **he stayed behind in the brothel in her clothes** after letting her out; and his answer at the scaffold, „Возљубљена сестро, не спречавај ме да умрем за Христа и крвљу мојом оперем грехе моје!“ **He also dies the same death in both books** — beheaded, body burnt — which is the one point of the execution the two agree on.

death.note: Охридски пролог за 09.06.2026 (27. мај ст. ст.): „Чесно пострадаше и задобише венце вечне славе 304. године у Александрији“. The first year any calendar read for this folder states; saint.gr gives none. The entry opens „У време злочестивог цара Максимилијана“ where saint.gr puts the martyrdom under Diocletian; both reigns are recorded in the life and no year was derived from either.
